subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: A straight line parallel to the line y = √3x passes through Q(2, 3) and cuts the line 2x + 4y − 27 = 0 at P. Find the length of PQ.

mark_split.label: Put P on the given line

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Long Answer question 19, book p.160. recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say how the parallel line gives you the angle, and what r means at the end.

steps.label: Find the inclination
steps.margin_note: First mark. Parallel lines have the same slope, so the given line hands over tan θ directly. The parametric form needs θ itself, not the slope.
lines: The line is parallel to y = √3x
Parallel lines have equal slopes, so

recall.must_convey: That the parallel line gives slope √3, so the inclination is 60°.
accept: parallel lines have the same slope so tan theta is root three
theta is sixty degrees
read the slope off y equals root three x
parallel kabatti same slope, theta sixty degrees
get the angle from the slope root three

steps.why: The parametric form needs an ANGLE, and a parallel line supplies it through its slope, so converting tan θ = √3 into θ = 60° is the first move.
common_mistakes: Using √3 in place of cos θ or sin θ.
Taking θ as 30° by reading the slope upside down.
steps.memory_tip: Parallel means the SAME slope, so the given line hands over tan θ straight away.

steps.label: Write the parametric point
steps.margin_note: The next two marks. Q is the base point and r is the unknown distance, so P is (x₁ + r cos θ, y₁ + r sin θ) with the 60° values put in.
lines: Let PQ = r and Q(x₁, y₁) = (2, 3)
P = (x₁ + r cos θ, y₁ + r sin θ)

recall.must_convey: That P is written as (2 + r/2, 3 + √3r/2) using the parametric form.
accept: P is x one plus r cos theta comma y one plus r sin theta
P is two plus r by two comma three plus root three r by two
write the parametric point with Q as the base
parametric form lo P rayali
put cos sixty and sin sixty into the parametric form

steps.why: One unknown r replaces two unknown coordinates, so the substitution below produces a single equation instead of a pair.
common_mistakes: Swapping cos θ and sin θ between the two coordinates.
steps.memory_tip: A point at distance r along the line is (x₁ + r cos θ, y₁ + r sin θ).

steps.label: Put P on the given line
steps.margin_note: The next two marks. P is on 2x + 4y − 27 = 0, so substituting turns the geometry into one equation in r. Distribute both coefficients across both parts.

recall.must_convey: That the parametric coordinates are substituted into 2x + 4y − 27 = 0.
accept: substitute the parametric point into the given line
P lies on the line so put its coordinates in
collect the r terms and the constants
P ni line lo substitute cheyyali
this gives one equation in r

steps.why: This is the only place the second line is used, so the substitution is what actually locates P.
common_mistakes: Multiplying 4 into only one part of the second coordinate.
Losing the √3 while collecting the r terms.
steps.memory_tip: P lies on the given line, so substituting leaves one equation in r alone.

steps.label: Solve for r
steps.margin_note: Two more marks. Both r terms are linear, so take r out as a common factor and divide once.

recall.must_convey: That r is taken out as a common factor to give r = 11/(2√3 + 1).
accept: take r common and divide
r into one plus two root three equals eleven
r is eleven over two root three plus one
r common teesi divide cheyyali
solve the linear equation for r

steps.why: The equation is linear in r even though it carries a surd, so one division finishes it — no quadratic and no second root.
common_mistakes: Squaring the equation, which is not needed and creates a false second root.
steps.memory_tip: Both r terms are linear, so take r common and divide once.

steps.label: Rationalise and state PQ
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Multiply above and below by the conjugate (2√3 − 1). The denominator becomes 12 − 1 = 11, which cancels the 11 on top exactly.

recall.must_convey: That rationalising by the conjugate gives PQ = 2√3 − 1 units.
accept: multiply above and below by two root three minus one
the denominator becomes twelve minus one which is eleven
P Q is two root three minus one
conjugate tho rationalise cheyyali
rationalise the denominator to finish

steps.why: A surd left in a denominator is not a finished answer, and here the conjugate cancels the 11 exactly, so the distance comes out in whole surd form.
common_mistakes: Using (2√3 + 1) again instead of the conjugate.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply by the conjugate: (2√3)² − 1² = 11, which cancels the 11 on top.
